t: Decode the Message — Substitution Table Construction
o: Scan key left to right, assigning 'a','b','c',... to each newly seen letter; this builds the cipher-to-plain map. Then translate message, leaving spaces untouched. Both strings are at most 2000 characters, so a single pass each is plenty. Example: key 'happy boy' maps h->a, a->b, p->c, y->d, b->e, o->f, etc.
k: First occurrence order in key defines the substitution alphabet directly.

a.n: Approach 1: Hash Map Build then Translate
a.i: One pass over key fills a 26-entry map from key letters to successive alphabet letters; one pass over message emits decoded characters.
s: Iterate key; for unseen lowercase letters assign map[ch] = chr(ord('a') + counter++).
Iterate message; append map[ch] or space.

w: Straightforward; the only care point is skipping spaces when building the table and preserving them in the output. No notable follow-ups beyond varying alphabets.
